mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes G Class G 350 d engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes G Class G 350 d engine replacement typically costs between £4,800 and £7,500 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt OM642 units range from £4,800 to £7,500 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £2,500-£4,000 but higher risk. Reconditioned units: £4,200-£6,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM642 oil cooler seal failure in a G 350 d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642's oil cooler seals typically fail between 60,000-90,000 miles, with tell-tale signs including oil spots under the vehicle and coolant contamination. Oil drips on the ground beneath the engine bay, particularly towards the rear. Oil in the coolant expansion tank (may appear as a milky or oily film). External oil weeping from the V-angle of the engine. Low oil level warnings between services.

mainEntity.name: Is the OM642 engine in the G 350 d reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 is generally robust but has a known weak point - the oil cooler seals fail on a significant proportion of units after 60,000 miles. Address this preventatively and the engine easily exceeds 150,000 miles. Oil cooler seal failure is the most common G 350 d issue. Post-2015 engines have improved single-row timing chains that are more durable. Regular oil changes with correct 229.51/229.52 spec oil are critical. With preventative maintenance, 200,000+ miles is realistic.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my G 350 d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., oil cooler seals, EGR cooler, turbo VNT cleaning). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or multiple major failures. Oil cooler seal replacement at specialist: £900-£1,400 - excellent value if caught early. EGR cooler replacement: £700-£1,100 - sensible repair for 80k+ mile cars. Full OM642 rebuild: £4,800-£7,500 - for catastrophic failure or 150k+ miles. Given G 350 d values (£25,000-£60,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my G 350 d has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix (e.g., OM642). V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block (visible from under vehicle). G 350 d (W463, 2015-2018): OM642.887. G 350 d (W464, 2018-2023): OM642 LS or OM642.887. Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used G 350 d engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a G 350 d. The complex 4MATIC system, gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. 4MATIC transfer case alignment requires specialist jigs. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation needed. Engine and gearbox must be separated correctly. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz G 350 d arrived in 2015 as the facelifted W463 generation's updated diesel flagship, replacing the G 350 CDI with a more powerful iteration of the OM642 V6 diesel - and later transitioned to the W464 generation with the same engine before being phased out in favour of the OM656 inline-six in the G 400 d.

milestones.description: G 350 d introduced with W463 facelift, OM642.887 3.0L V6 diesel, 245hp, Euro 6 emissions compliance
2018 - W463 G 350 d production, 7G-TRONIC PLUS automatic transmission, 600Nm torque
W464 all-new G-Class launched, G 350 d continues with OM642 V6 diesel in the new platform
2023 - W464 G 350 d production continues with OM642, later phased out as G 400 d (OM656 inline-six) became the primary diesel offering

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d relies on the OM642 V6 diesel - a generally robust engine that has developed a well-documented reputation for specific failures. The oil cooler seal issue dominates replacement demand, while EGR cooler and turbocharger-related problems also drive repair enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common G 350 d engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Failure - Why the G 350 d Leaks Oil Excessively
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d (OM642.887, OM642 LS, 2015-2023)
problems.rootCause: The factory rubber oil cooler seals harden and shrink due to heat cycling, allowing oil to mix with coolant and external oil leaks to form at the V-angle of the engine. Mercedes Service Bulletin LI18.30-P-055434 addresses this known issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil cooler seals (revised parts), flush cooling system, new oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles if using revised Viton seals

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace complete oil cooler unit with revised seals, coolant flush, thermostat inspection
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; recommended if cooler shows corrosion

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 with upgraded seals, new oil pump chain, turbo inspected

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 350 d is worth £25,000-£60,000 depending on age, mileage and condition - the full replacement cost of £4,800-£7,500 is modest relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine excellent value. For vehicles worth under £10,000 (high-mileage examples), evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: If caught early with only external weeping, the seal-only specialist fix at £900-£1,400 is excellent value and should last 60k+ miles with revised seals. However, if the leak has caused coolant contamination or the engine has overheated, we recommend the full rebuilt route - contaminated oil galleries often cause turbo or bearing failure within 10k-15k miles of a partial repair.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d engine prices

problems.h4: OM642 EGR Cooler Failure - Why the G 350 d Loses Coolant and Triggers Emissions Faults
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d (OM642.887, OM642 LS, 2015-2023)
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can crack internally, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust system - triggering low coolant warnings, white smoke, and emissions-related fault codes. Carbon buildup also causes the EGR valve to stick open or closed.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve, clear carbon deposits, reset adaptations
Replace EGR cooler, new gaskets, coolant flush, system bleed
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles; recommended if coolant loss detected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 with new EGR cooler, upgraded seals
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic failure or 150k+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a G 350 d worth £25,000-£60,000, the EGR cooler replacement at £700-£1,100 is a sensible repair. The full engine replacement cost is only justified if there is additional damage or the engine has high mileage.
problems.recommendation: On a G 350 d with 80k+ miles, we recommend having the EGR system inspected during any major service. If the cooler is leaking, specialist replacement at £700-£1,100 is the right call - don't ignore coolant loss, as it can lead to overheating and more extensive engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d engine prices

problems.h4: OM642 Turbocharger & Timing Chain Wear - High-Mileage G 350 d Concerns
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 d (OM642.887, OM642 LS, 2015-2023)
problems.rootCause: The variable geometry turbocharger can suffer from sticking vanes due to carbon buildup, while the timing chain can stretch on very high-mileage units - though the later single-row chain fitted from 2015 is considerably more durable than earlier dual-row versions.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean turbo variable vanes, recalibrate actuator
Replace turbocharger, new oil lines, gaskets, recalibrate
repairOptions.longevity: 120k-180k miles; if VNT cleaning no longer resolves issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 with new turbo, timing chain, upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required for catastrophic turbo failure or 180k+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 350 d worth £25,000-£60,000, turbocharger replacement at £1,200-£1,800 is a justifiable repair. Timing chain replacement is rarely needed before 200,000 miles on the later OM642 units.
problems.recommendation: The OM642's timing chain is not a major concern on post-2015 G 350 d models - as one specialist notes, "unless you intend to drive it past 200K miles, I wouldn't worry about it." For turbo issues, start with VNT cleaning before committing to a full replacement - many sticking vane problems can be resolved without removing the turbo.
